gaps.text: In-line measurement of Process temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one calibration model per method, then fuse the Raman and mid-IR variables with block scaling so that neither block dominates the model. Both methods must look at the same small volume of the medium at the same time - a combined probe is the practical route - and the data must be normalised to a common time step. Each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)

items.finding: The source states that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an aqueous cell culture medium, this suggests temperature should be controlled or monitored during spectral measurement to reduce OH-band variation; a temperature sensor could be tested alongside the probe.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns NIR and MIR, not Raman, and refers to tempered sample holders rather than an in-line process temperature sensor; transfer to a pilot cell culture is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: The source says acid concentrations, ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This could support including temperature as a varied factor in calibration and monitoring it during runs, so the model is not fitted to a single temperature.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work is on reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not cell culture, and does not describe an in-line temperature sensor.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19
